items.title: UI dispatches catalogued typed commands only
items.statement: The UI boundary accepts only typed UICommand messages with stable command IDs sourced from the command catalog.

evidence.exact_quote: The UI layer MUST dispatch only typed `UICommand` messages whose `command_id` values are stable IDs drawn from `Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md`.

items.title: View layer has no backend mutation authority
items.statement: The UI cannot directly call backend services, storage, or domain logic and cannot mutate backend state; it emits commands and renders projected state.

evidence.exact_quote: - The UI MUST NOT call backend services, storage, or domain logic directly.
- No backend mutation may originate from the view layer; the view layer is a pure function of projected state plus outbound `UICommand` emissions.

items.title: Every interactive element has exactly one matrix command mapping
items.statement: Each interactive UI element maps to exactly one UICommandID, and every element must have a wiring-matrix entry.

evidence.exact_quote: Every interactive UI element (button, menu item, link, toggle, slider, form submit) MUST map to exactly one `UICommandID`.
- No interactive element may exist without a corresponding wiring matrix entry.

items.title: Orphan elements and commands fail the gate
items.statement: Both interactive elements without wiring entries and catalog commands without handlers are gate failures.

evidence.exact_quote: - Orphan elements (interactive elements with no wiring entry) and orphan commands (catalog entries with no handler) are both gate failures.

items.title: Command-to-projection data flow is explicit
items.statement: Interaction creates an envelope, the dispatcher routes it, the handler executes domain logic and emits persisted events, projections derive state, and the UI observes that state.

dimension_assessments.summary: Approval gating, command dispatch, handler execution, event emission, projection, and UI observation behavior are explicit.
The window defines UI command dispatch, wiring verification, disabled-reason projection, and autonomous gating capabilities.
Primary inputs and outputs are named, but envelope typing and correlation identity are not executable contracts.
Strong boundary and matrix contracts exist, but error shape, envelope typing, and handler lifecycle/gate scoping remain incomplete or conflicting.
Disabled, command, event, projection, and handler lifecycle states are defined, but report failure/freshness and command delivery recovery transitions are absent.
The view/dispatcher/backend boundary, product-owner references, and non-overridable gate authority are explicit.
UI wiring ownership and downstream product-semantic owners are identified, including handler owner_doc_ref for planned rows.
UI, dispatcher, handlers, projections, gates, and Instant Grep wiring are identified as consumers or participants.
GUI enablement, purity, and element wiring are explicit, but disabled-reason presentation remains discretionary.
Unknown commands and gate failures are covered, but report failure, error projection, retry, idempotency, timeout, and partial-event recovery are not.
No authorization checkpoint or sensitive-argument redaction rule is stated in this window; an external contract may own it, but that cannot be established from the authorized excerpt.
Command-to-event-to-projection propagation is explicit, while duplicate, ordering, and partial-failure propagation semantics are absent.
Verification is autonomous, deterministic, progression-blocking, and evidence-producing.
The architecture has no queueing, concurrency, ordering, backpressure, overload, or latency contract in this window.
Migration provenance and scope are recorded, but stable ID and schema evolution rules are missing.
GATE-010 supplies broad deterministic checks, yet row-level acceptance_checks and evidence_required grammar is under-specified and handler-state scoping conflicts.
Consequential discretion remains in report recovery/freshness, GUI formatting, envelope/error shape, handler-state gating, delivery semantics, security, performance, and migration.
The `/lenient` token is ambiguous, and security/privacy ownership is unknown from this authorized window.
